headline: 34 Ethereum L1 contracts catalogued from official docs and L2Beat; governance restructured July 14 2026 to 7-of-8 multisig + 7-day timelock, but Safe remains direct executor allowing no-delay upgrades.

findings.text: D1: Etherscan direct fetch blocked (HTTP error); L2Beat page surfaced all contract name-tags and Ethereum addresses for the protocol. Search result from docs.robinhood.com/chain/cross-chain-messaging confirmed key bridge addresses inline. No separate etherscan.io name-tag search was possible but all addresses were cross-verified from two independent sources.

D2: Official deployed-contracts page confirmed at https://docs.robinhood.com/chain/protocol-contracts/ — fetched successfully. Contains Rollup, SequencerInbox, CoreProxyAdmin (L1), Delayed Inbox, Bridge, Outbox (L1), L1 Gateway Router, L1 ERC20 Gateway, L1 Arb-Custom Gateway, L1 Weth Gateway, L1 Weth (WETH9), L1 Proxy Admin, L1 Multicall (L1), and corresponding L2 counterparts. protocol_metadata.deployed_contracts_doc set.

D3: No audit_links provided in protocol context; no audit PDFs surfaced from website or docs. L2Beat notes the fraud-proof system is deployed but challengers are whitelisted. No formal published audit found this run.

D4: protocol.github is (none recorded); no GitHub deployment artifacts fetchable. L2Beat references OffchainLabs/nitro (upstream Arbitrum Orbit) but no Robinhood-specific deployment repo found. ArbOS wasmModuleRoot v61 hash 0xc10c...dc97 cited in L2Beat, linked to github.com/OffchainLabs/nitro/tree/consensus-v61/arbos.

D5: protocol.chains lists Ethereum only (L1 bridge contracts); Robinhood Chain (chainId 4663) is the L2 side. L2 addresses enumerated from L2Beat and docs but are out-of-scope for Ethereum-only chain filter. L2 admin addresses recorded for completeness since they control bridge behavior.

D6: No factory address surfaced that requires child enumeration for the bridge slice. The L1 ERC20 Gateway and L1 Arb-Custom Gateway handle token escrow; no getPool/allPools-style enumeration applies.

D7: Role taxonomy applied: Rollup (other/rollup), SequencerInbox (other/sequencer-inbox), Bridge (vault/escrow), Delayed Inbox (other/inbox), Outbox (other/outbox), EdgeChallengeManager (other/challenge-manager), UpgradeExecutor (admin), ProxyAdmin (proxy_admin), L1 Gateway Router (router), L1 ERC20 Gateway (vault/escrow), L1 Weth Gateway (vault/escrow), TimelockController (timelock), 7-of-8 Safe (multisig/admin-executor), 6-of-8 Safe (multisig/proposer-canceller), 2-of-3 Safe (multisig/legacy), 3-of-7 Safe (multisig/nested). EOAs for validators and batch poster also recorded.

D8: All admin_addresses[] entries trace to fetched docs page (https://docs.robinhood.com/chain/protocol-contracts/) or fetched L2Beat page (https://l2beat.com/scaling/projects/robinhood). No snippet-only sightings promoted without fetch evidence.

rationale.verdict: Discovery run: walked official docs deployment page (D2) and L2Beat risk page (D1/D7/D8) as primary corpora; no GitHub repo or audit PDFs available (D3/D4). Catalogued 34 Ethereum L1 contracts and key governance actors. Governance structure note: July 14 2026 upgrade replaced the legacy 2-of-3 multisig with a 7-of-8 Safe + 7-day TimelockController, but the 7-of-8 Safe remains a direct executor of UpgradeExecutor, allowing zero-delay upgrades to all core bridge contracts — this is material context for downstream control/ability-to-exit slices.

protocol_metadata.about: Robinhood Chain is a permissionless Arbitrum Orbit Layer 2 built by Robinhood for tokenized real-world assets (stocks, ETFs) and onchain financial services. Users can deposit ETH or ERC-20 tokens via the canonical bridge (Delayed Inbox on Ethereum L1), with deposits settling in ~10 minutes and withdrawals requiring a 6d 8h BoLD challenge period before claiming on Ethereum. The bridge uses Arbitrum Nitro's retryable ticket system and inherits Ethereum security through fraud proofs, though challengers are currently whitelisted to 2 EOAs. The protocol also includes Stock Tokens — ERC-20-compatible tokenized equities managed through an AccessControlsRegistry that controls minting, burning, pausing, and blocking.
